questions.question: How does N-bromosuccinimide (NBS) maintain a low steady-state concentration of molecular Br₂ during allylic bromination?

options.label: A
options.text: NBS dissolves all bromine into the gas phase.

options.label: B
options.text: NBS reacts rapidly with trace HBr generated in the reaction to produce Br₂ at low steady-state concentrations, favoring radical substitution over ionic addition.

options.label: C
options.text: NBS acts as a Lewis acid that destroys bromine.

options.label: D
options.text: NBS completely prevents HBr from forming.

questions.correct_answer: NBS reacts rapidly with trace HBr generated in the reaction to produce Br₂ at low steady-state concentrations, favoring radical substitution over ionic addition.
questions.explanation: Maintaining extremely low [Br₂] prevents ionic electrophilic addition across the double bond, ensuring selective allylic radical substitution.

questions.question: Why is the activation energy for allylic C-H hydrogen abstraction (~360 kJ/mol) significantly lower than for aliphatic C-H (~410 kJ/mol)?

options.label: A
options.text: The alkene π bond repels the incoming radical initiator.

options.label: B
options.text: Allylic C-H bonds are ionic rather than covalent.

options.label: C
options.text: Allylic radicals form three-membered cyclic rings.

options.label: D
options.text: The developing allylic radical in the transition state is stabilized by continuous orbital overlap with the adjacent alkene π bond across three sp² carbons.

questions.correct_answer: The developing allylic radical in the transition state is stabilized by continuous orbital overlap with the adjacent alkene π bond across three sp² carbons.
questions.explanation: Delocalization of the unpaired electron across the 3-carbon π system lowers the bond dissociation energy and transition state energy.

questions.question: How many resonance structures distribute the unpaired electron in a benzyl radical (PhCH₂•)?

options.label: A
options.text: Two structures involving meta positions.

options.label: B
options.text: Only one localized structure.

options.label: C
options.text: Four resonance structures: one benzylic structure and three ortho/para cyclohexadienyl radical contributors.

options.label: D
options.text: Six structures with ring expansion to tropylium.

questions.correct_answer: Four resonance structures: one benzylic structure and three ortho/para cyclohexadienyl radical contributors.
questions.explanation: The unpaired electron is delocalized onto the benzylic carbon and the ortho and para positions of the aromatic ring.

questions.question: Why is radical bromination highly regioselective for tertiary positions (1600:1 vs 1°) while chlorination is unselective (5:1 vs 1°)?

options.label: A
options.text: Chlorine radicals cannot abstract primary hydrogens.

options.label: B
options.text: Bromination hydrogen abstraction is endothermic with a late transition state resembling the radical intermediate (Hammond postulate), whereas chlorination is exothermic with an early TS.

options.label: C
options.text: Bromine radicals react via ionic mechanisms.

options.label: D
options.text: Chlorine radicals are sterically much larger than bromine radicals.

questions.correct_answer: Bromination hydrogen abstraction is endothermic with a late transition state resembling the radical intermediate (Hammond postulate), whereas chlorination is exothermic with an early TS.
questions.explanation: Endothermic abstraction by bromine creates a late transition state that fully senses differences in radical intermediate stabilities.

questions.topic: Radical Addition of HBr to Alkenes (Peroxide Effect)
questions.question: Why does the 'peroxide effect' reverse the regioselectivity of HBr addition to alkenes, but fails for HCl and HI?

options.label: A
options.text: HCl and HI are insoluble in peroxides.

options.label: B
options.text: Both propagation steps are exothermic for HBr, whereas hydrogen abstraction is endothermic for HI and halogen radical addition is endothermic for HCl.

options.label: C
options.text: HCl forms carbocations exclusively under all conditions.

options.label: D
options.text: Peroxides only react with bromine atoms.

questions.correct_answer: Both propagation steps are exothermic for HBr, whereas hydrogen abstraction is endothermic for HI and halogen radical addition is endothermic for HCl.
questions.explanation: Radical chain propagation is thermodynamically feasible only when both propagation steps have favorable negative or near-zero free energies (unique to HBr).

questions.question: What is the elementary step that drives polymer chain growth in the radical polymerization of styrene?

options.label: A
options.text: Coupling of two polymer radicals with loss of hydrogen.

options.label: B
options.text: Addition of the carbon-centered benzyl radical to the less substituted carbon of a styrene monomer, regenerating a stable benzylic radical at the chain end.

options.label: C
options.text: Elimination of phenyl radicals into the solvent.

options.label: D
options.text: Proton transfer from the initiator to the monomer.

questions.correct_answer: Addition of the carbon-centered benzyl radical to the less substituted carbon of a styrene monomer, regenerating a stable benzylic radical at the chain end.
questions.explanation: Chain propagation proceeds by repeated addition of the propagating radical to monomer double bonds, regenerating the active radical center.

questions.question: What is the hazardous intermediate formed when diethyl ether is exposed to atmospheric oxygen and light over time?

options.label: A
options.text: A harmless dimer of diethyl ether.

options.label: B
options.text: Gaseous carbon dioxide and methane.

options.label: C
options.text: An explosive hydroperoxide [CH₃CH(OOH)OCH₂CH₃] formed by radical abstraction of the weak α-ethereal C-H bond followed by O₂ trapping.

options.label: D
options.text: Pure liquid ethanol.

questions.correct_answer: An explosive hydroperoxide [CH₃CH(OOH)OCH₂CH₃] formed by radical abstraction of the weak α-ethereal C-H bond followed by O₂ trapping.
questions.explanation: The α-hydrogens adjacent to ether oxygen are easily abstracted by radicals, initiating autooxidation to explosive organic hydroperoxides.

questions.question: How does butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT) chemically inhibit radical chain degradation in foods and polymers?

options.label: A
options.text: BHT reacts with water to form sulfuric acid.

options.label: B
options.text: BHT destroys all oxygen molecules in the mixture.

options.label: C
options.text: BHT donates a phenolic hydrogen to propagating radicals, forming a sterically hindered phenoxy radical that is too unreactive to propagate chain reactions.

options.label: D
options.text: BHT acts as a photochemical shield reflecting UV light.

questions.correct_answer: BHT donates a phenolic hydrogen to propagating radicals, forming a sterically hindered phenoxy radical that is too unreactive to propagate chain reactions.
questions.explanation: The resulting hindered phenoxy radical is stabilized by resonance and sterically shielded by two tert-butyl groups, halting radical chain propagation.

questions.question: What is the role of AIBN in the Barton radical dehalogenation using Bu₃SnH?

options.label: A
options.text: AIBN acts as a strong Lewis acid catalyst.

options.label: B
options.text: AIBN coordinates to the alkyl halide to form an onium salt.

options.label: C
options.text: AIBN undergoes thermal homolysis to generate isobutyronitrile radicals that abstract hydrogen from Bu₃SnH, generating the chain-propagating Bu₃Sn• radical.

options.label: D
options.text: AIBN reduces the alkyl halide via SN2.

questions.correct_answer: AIBN undergoes thermal homolysis to generate isobutyronitrile radicals that abstract hydrogen from Bu₃SnH, generating the chain-propagating Bu₃Sn• radical.
questions.explanation: AIBN is a radical initiator that homolytically cleaves with loss of N₂ gas to launch the radical chain cycle.

questions.question: What are the two competing pathways for radical chain termination when two alkyl radicals collide?

options.label: A
options.text: Oxidation to carboxylic acids and reduction to alcohols.

options.label: B
options.text: Electrocyclic ring opening and cyclization.

options.label: C
options.text: Ionization into carbocations and precipitation as salts.

options.label: D
options.text: Combination (covalent C-C coupling) and Disproportionation (hydrogen transfer from one radical to the other, yielding an alkane and an alkene).

questions.correct_answer: Combination (covalent C-C coupling) and Disproportionation (hydrogen transfer from one radical to the other, yielding an alkane and an alkene).
questions.explanation: Two radicals can terminate either by direct coupling to form a longer alkane or by hydrogen abstraction to form an alkane/alkene pair.

questions.question: Why is radical bromination highly regioselective for tertiary positions (1600:1 vs 1°) while chlorination is unselective (5:1 vs 1°)?

options.label: A
options.text: Chlorine radicals are sterically much larger than bromine radicals.

options.label: B
options.text: Chlorine radicals cannot abstract primary hydrogens.

options.label: C
options.text: Bromine radicals react via ionic mechanisms.

options.label: D
options.text: Bromination hydrogen abstraction is endothermic with a late transition state resembling the radical intermediate (Hammond postulate), whereas chlorination is exothermic with an early TS.

questions.correct_answer: Bromination hydrogen abstraction is endothermic with a late transition state resembling the radical intermediate (Hammond postulate), whereas chlorination is exothermic with an early TS.
questions.explanation: Endothermic abstraction by bromine creates a late transition state that fully senses differences in radical intermediate stabilities.

questions.topic: Radical Addition of HBr to Alkenes (Peroxide Effect)
questions.question: Why does the 'peroxide effect' reverse the regioselectivity of HBr addition to alkenes, but fails for HCl and HI?

options.label: A
options.text: Both propagation steps are exothermic for HBr, whereas hydrogen abstraction is endothermic for HI and halogen radical addition is endothermic for HCl.

options.label: B
options.text: Peroxides only react with bromine atoms.

options.label: C
options.text: HCl forms carbocations exclusively under all conditions.

options.label: D
options.text: HCl and HI are insoluble in peroxides.

questions.correct_answer: Both propagation steps are exothermic for HBr, whereas hydrogen abstraction is endothermic for HI and halogen radical addition is endothermic for HCl.
questions.explanation: Radical chain propagation is thermodynamically feasible only when both propagation steps have favorable negative or near-zero free energies (unique to HBr).

questions.question: What is the elementary step that drives polymer chain growth in the radical polymerization of styrene?

options.label: A
options.text: Coupling of two polymer radicals with loss of hydrogen.

options.label: B
options.text: Proton transfer from the initiator to the monomer.

options.label: C
options.text: Elimination of phenyl radicals into the solvent.

options.label: D
options.text: Addition of the carbon-centered benzyl radical to the less substituted carbon of a styrene monomer, regenerating a stable benzylic radical at the chain end.

questions.correct_answer: Addition of the carbon-centered benzyl radical to the less substituted carbon of a styrene monomer, regenerating a stable benzylic radical at the chain end.
questions.explanation: Chain propagation proceeds by repeated addition of the propagating radical to monomer double bonds, regenerating the active radical center.

questions.question: What is the role of AIBN in the Barton radical dehalogenation using Bu₃SnH?

options.label: A
options.text: AIBN coordinates to the alkyl halide to form an onium salt.

options.label: B
options.text: AIBN reduces the alkyl halide via SN2.

options.label: C
options.text: AIBN undergoes thermal homolysis to generate isobutyronitrile radicals that abstract hydrogen from Bu₃SnH, generating the chain-propagating Bu₃Sn• radical.

options.label: D
options.text: AIBN acts as a strong Lewis acid catalyst.

questions.correct_answer: AIBN undergoes thermal homolysis to generate isobutyronitrile radicals that abstract hydrogen from Bu₃SnH, generating the chain-propagating Bu₃Sn• radical.
questions.explanation: AIBN is a radical initiator that homolytically cleaves with loss of N₂ gas to launch the radical chain cycle.

questions.question: What are the two competing pathways for radical chain termination when two alkyl radicals collide?

options.label: A
options.text: Ionization into carbocations and precipitation as salts.

options.label: B
options.text: Electrocyclic ring opening and cyclization.

options.label: C
options.text: Combination (covalent C-C coupling) and Disproportionation (hydrogen transfer from one radical to the other, yielding an alkane and an alkene).

options.label: D
options.text: Oxidation to carboxylic acids and reduction to alcohols.

questions.correct_answer: Combination (covalent C-C coupling) and Disproportionation (hydrogen transfer from one radical to the other, yielding an alkane and an alkene).
questions.explanation: Two radicals can terminate either by direct coupling to form a longer alkane or by hydrogen abstraction to form an alkane/alkene pair.

questions.question: How does N-bromosuccinimide (NBS) maintain a low steady-state concentration of molecular Br₂ during allylic bromination?

options.label: A
options.text: NBS completely prevents HBr from forming.

options.label: B
options.text: NBS reacts rapidly with trace HBr generated in the reaction to produce Br₂ at low steady-state concentrations, favoring radical substitution over ionic addition.

options.label: C
options.text: NBS acts as a Lewis acid that destroys bromine.

options.label: D
options.text: NBS dissolves all bromine into the gas phase.

questions.correct_answer: NBS reacts rapidly with trace HBr generated in the reaction to produce Br₂ at low steady-state concentrations, favoring radical substitution over ionic addition.
questions.explanation: Maintaining extremely low [Br₂] prevents ionic electrophilic addition across the double bond, ensuring selective allylic radical substitution.

questions.question: Why is the activation energy for allylic C-H hydrogen abstraction (~360 kJ/mol) significantly lower than for aliphatic C-H (~410 kJ/mol)?

options.label: A
options.text: Allylic radicals form three-membered cyclic rings.

options.label: B
options.text: The alkene π bond repels the incoming radical initiator.

options.label: C
options.text: The developing allylic radical in the transition state is stabilized by continuous orbital overlap with the adjacent alkene π bond across three sp² carbons.

options.label: D
options.text: Allylic C-H bonds are ionic rather than covalent.

questions.correct_answer: The developing allylic radical in the transition state is stabilized by continuous orbital overlap with the adjacent alkene π bond across three sp² carbons.
questions.explanation: Delocalization of the unpaired electron across the 3-carbon π system lowers the bond dissociation energy and transition state energy.

questions.question: What is the hazardous intermediate formed when diethyl ether is exposed to atmospheric oxygen and light over time?

options.label: A
options.text: Gaseous carbon dioxide and methane.

options.label: B
options.text: Pure liquid ethanol.

options.label: C
options.text: An explosive hydroperoxide [CH₃CH(OOH)OCH₂CH₃] formed by radical abstraction of the weak α-ethereal C-H bond followed by O₂ trapping.

options.label: D
options.text: A harmless dimer of diethyl ether.

questions.correct_answer: An explosive hydroperoxide [CH₃CH(OOH)OCH₂CH₃] formed by radical abstraction of the weak α-ethereal C-H bond followed by O₂ trapping.
questions.explanation: The α-hydrogens adjacent to ether oxygen are easily abstracted by radicals, initiating autooxidation to explosive organic hydroperoxides.

questions.question: How does butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT) chemically inhibit radical chain degradation in foods and polymers?

options.label: A
options.text: BHT destroys all oxygen molecules in the mixture.

options.label: B
options.text: BHT acts as a photochemical shield reflecting UV light.

options.label: C
options.text: BHT donates a phenolic hydrogen to propagating radicals, forming a sterically hindered phenoxy radical that is too unreactive to propagate chain reactions.

options.label: D
options.text: BHT reacts with water to form sulfuric acid.

questions.correct_answer: BHT donates a phenolic hydrogen to propagating radicals, forming a sterically hindered phenoxy radical that is too unreactive to propagate chain reactions.
questions.explanation: The resulting hindered phenoxy radical is stabilized by resonance and sterically shielded by two tert-butyl groups, halting radical chain propagation.
